text: Recovery Workbench Batch and Scheduling Design v5 and Recovery Workbench Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1 are issued with no approval recorded, in Draft status.
why: This run is the D-RCV-60 realignment: no human approval step is available, the run must not stop for one, and the overlay records the missing approval as an assumption.
read: Both documents are complete and may be cited by the architecture, requirements and story documents of this run; the approval is recorded afterwards by the owner of each document.
applied_in: Batch and Scheduling Design v5, sheet Read me, row 23; Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1, sheet Read me
impact: A document that stories cite for their section 12.5 and 12.6 contracts carries Draft status until the approval is recorded.

text: Batch and Scheduling Design v5 keeps every v4 row, ID, job name, time, dependency, failure rule, owner role and TimerScheduler value unchanged in columns A to H, rewrites only the two description rows of the Jobs sheet, and adds the realignment in columns I to N and in two new sheets.
why: The work package requires the next version to keep every section, ID, number and date of the source and to change only what the realignment needs; a reader must still be able to compare a v5 row with v4 without opening the older file.
read: The v4 text of a job is readable in the same row as its v5 owner, mechanism, workflow or Schedule, task queue and source; the two description rows state the v5 mechanism and keep the v4 numbers.
applied_in: Batch and Scheduling Design v5, sheet Jobs, columns A to H and N, rows 2 and 3; sheet Read me rows 11 to 16
impact: The document carries both readings of each job, so a build team cannot mistake a v4 Quartz mechanism for the target mechanism.

text: JOB-10 WIN notices is a Temporal Schedule in rwb-comms at 16:00 that starts the notice dispatch and calls deliverFile in rwb-integration, with the bank's Airflow opening the WIN file window at 16:00.
why: Architecture v5 slide 44 gives the mechanism as 'Airflow file window + workers' and slide 31 notes list the WIN letters at 16:00 among the Temporal Schedules; the ownership map rules for rwb-comms (P6) as the one owner, with rwb-integration (P2) performing the file step.
read: rwb-comms owns the notice, the 16:00 trigger and the Schedule; rwb-integration owns deliverFile and the file window handshake; neither service reads the other's schema.
applied_in: Batch and Scheduling Design v5, sheet Jobs row JOB-10; Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1, sheet Schedules row JOB-10
impact: If the file window is the trigger and not the Schedule, the 16:00 Schedule moves to rwb-integration and the notice becomes an activity there; the owner of JOB-10 changes.

text: JOB-15 reporting extract is triggered by the bank's Airflow at 01:30 through POST /reports/{id}/run on rwb-reporting, which runs the buildRegulatoryExtract activity from the service's own projections, with no data lake.
why: Architecture v5 slide 44 gives the mechanism as 'Airflow trigger (no data lake)' and slide 32 places the extract at 01:30 through the reporting API; the data lake and INT-19 and INT-20 are removed under DP-17.
read: rwb-reporting owns the extract and the activity; Airflow owns the trigger and the re-run by business date; a 01:30 Schedule named on slides 15 and 31 remains a documented alternative and is not configured.
applied_in: Batch and Scheduling Design v5, sheet Jobs row JOB-15 and sheet Daily timeline v5 block; Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1, sheet Activities row buildRegulatoryExtract
impact: If the 01:30 Schedule is the target, rwb-reporting needs a Schedule and the Airflow trigger becomes a manual re-run path; the reporting story's section 12.6 changes.

text: JOB-16 write-off scan is a Temporal Schedule in rwb-writeoff on the third working day of the month that starts WriteOffWorkflow, and the workflow itself checks AceDataReady for the business date before it scans.
why: Architecture v5 slide 44 and Temporal and Drools design slide 23 make JOB-16 a Schedule on the third working day in rwb-writeoff, while Batch and Scheduling Design v4 keeps it on the ACE batch-complete record for ALS; a cron expression cannot express a working-day gate on an event, so the gate sits in the workflow.
read: The Schedule fires on the third working day; if AceDataReady for that business date has not arrived, the workflow waits for it or exits with a recorded reason instead of scanning a stale business date.
applied_in: Batch and Scheduling Design v5, sheet Jobs row JOB-16; Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1, sheet Schedules row JOB-16
impact: If the ACE batch record stays the trigger, JOB-16 becomes an event-started workflow and the third-working-day rule moves into the event consumer.

text: The two event-started workflows of JOB-07 and JOB-08 are listed in the catalog as one row each, owned by rwb-payment (P8), started by AceDataReady, with matchPayments and confirmBookings as their only known activity, and the workflow name carried as the R9 placeholder.
why: Architecture v5 slide 44 makes both jobs event-started workflows in rwb-payment and no source names the workflow; naming one would invent a contract that the story files would then cite.
read: A build team knows the owner, the queue, the trigger and the activity of each job; the workflow name, ID and the one-or-two-workshop question stay open until CG-B-ARCH-WF-3 is settled.
applied_in: Batch and Scheduling Design v5, sheet Jobs rows JOB-07 and JOB-08; Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1, sheet Workflows rows 19 and 20
impact: The payment story of wave 2 cannot declare a workflow contract until the name is confirmed.

text: Where a Schedule starts work whose workflow or activity is not named, the catalog records the Schedule, the owner, the queue and the work the v4 row describes, and carries the workflow or activity as the R9 placeholder; the two rwb-source-data workflows AceIngestCheck and reconciliation are recorded as workflows with their activities as the placeholder.
why: The six Schedules and two workflows are named in Architecture v5 and Batch and Scheduling Design v4, but no source names what each one runs; the catalog must still give the build team a row per Schedule and per workflow.
read: The Schedule, its owner and its time are fixed; only the name of the started activity or workflow, and therefore the contract jar, stays open.
applied_in: Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1, sheet Schedules rows JOB-06, 14, 17, 18, 19; sheet Workflows rows AceIngestCheck and reconciliation
impact: Five Schedules and two workflows cannot be built to a contract until the names are confirmed; the Schedule definitions themselves are unaffected.

text: No Temporal Schedule ID, cron expression or per-Schedule overlap value is invented; each Schedule carries the name the source gives it and the Schedule ID cell holds the R9 placeholder.
why: No source gives an identifier or a calendar expression for any Schedule, and an invented identifier would be cited by stories and by the platform story as if it were agreed.
read: The ten Schedules are identified by their job and their source name until the platform team confirms the identifiers; the times and cadences are the v4 and Architecture v5 values, unchanged.
applied_in: Batch and Scheduling Design v5, sheet Schedule and event map, column Schedule ID; Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1, sheet Schedules, column Schedule ID
impact: Ten Schedules have no identifier in the catalog and cannot be deployed until CG-B-ARCH-WF-1 is settled.

text: The v4 Daily timeline rows are kept unchanged and a v5 block is added below them: JOB-13 is continuous ingest with no nightly copy, JOB-15 runs at 01:30 from Airflow and JOB-14 at 02:00 from its Schedule, so the v4 row '01:00 to 02:00' no longer describes the target.
why: The work package keeps every section, ID, number and date of the source, and the realignment moves three of the jobs that the v4 row groups together.
read: The v4 order of the day is readable for comparison; the v5 block is the order a build team implements, and the retirements of JOB-13 and JOB-15 are stated rather than implied.
applied_in: Batch and Scheduling Design v5, sheet Daily timeline, rows 13 to 31
impact: A reader who stops at the v4 rows sees a nightly data-lake copy that no longer exists; the v5 block immediately below corrects it.

text: Activity timeouts and heartbeat intervals are carried as the R9 placeholder in the catalog; the retry policy of 1 s initial interval, back-off 2 and 10 attempts is carried as the only fixed value.
why: Architecture v5 slide 11 names start-to-close per activity, backoff and heartbeats without a value for any activity, and an invented timeout would become a contract.
read: A build team knows the retry behaviour and the non-retryable failure of every activity; the timeout and heartbeat values stay open until the contract jars are written.
applied_in: Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1, sheet Activities, column Retry and timeout; sheet Platform rules, row 5
impact: No activity contract jar can be completed until the timeouts are set; the workflow code is unaffected.

text: DailyCaseRun is recorded as event-started by AceDataReady, with the Schedule that Architecture v5 slide 14 names beside the event kept as a documented fallback that is not configured in the target.
why: Architecture v5 slide 44 and the slide 31 notes make AceDataReady the trigger of the morning run, and slide 14 names a Schedule in the same cell without saying when it fires.
read: JOB-02 and JOB-03 run when the business date is signalled; a day without the signal has no automatic run until the fallback is confirmed.
applied_in: Batch and Scheduling Design v5, sheet Jobs row JOB-02 and sheet Schedule and event map row JOB-02; Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1, sheet Workflows row DailyCaseRun
impact: If the Schedule is the primary trigger, rwb-case needs a cron Schedule and an overlap policy, and the event becomes a second trigger that must be de-duplicated.

text: The platform worker that runs PlatformSmokeWorkflow and the stuck workflow scan is owned by PLT on task queue rwb-platform, which is outside the 19 service queues and has no schema of its own in the sources.
why: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 names the queue rwb-platform and Architecture v5 slide 44 gives the owner as platform; the Ownership Map has no service row for it and no source defines a schema.
read: JOB-21 and JOB-22 have an owner, a queue and a mechanism; the deployment, the schema and the quotas of that worker remain open.
applied_in: Batch and Scheduling Design v5, sheet Jobs rows JOB-21 and JOB-22 and sheet Schedule and event map; Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1, sheet Task queues and namespaces
impact: The platform story cannot declare a deployment or a database login for the rwb-platform worker until the owner confirms whether it needs one.

text: The CaseWorkflow workflow ID is recorded as the case ID, following the Temporal and Drools design, and the ADR-011 form case-{caseId} is recorded as the differing source in CG-B-ARCH-WF-7 until the architect confirms one form.
why: R-PREC puts the Temporal and Drools Detailed Design above the Architecture Decision Records, and the two forms are not interchangeable for signalWithStart or for the JOB-21 visibility query.
read: The case router, the stage child workflows and the stuck workflow scan use the case ID; an implementation that follows ADR-011 instead would create a second run for the same case.
applied_in: Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1, sheet Workflows row CaseWorkflow, column Started by; sheet Platform rules row 20
impact: A mismatch between the form used by the router and the form used by the child or the scan produces duplicate workflows or an empty stuck-case panel.
